newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Reliance commissions new plant.
newsitem.headline: India's Reliance commissions new plant.

text.p: Indian petrochemicals and textiles firm Reliance Industries Ltd said it commissioned a second production line at its polypropylene plant.
"With the commissioning of the second line, the company's production capacity in this product increased to 350,000 tonnes per year," it said in a statement on Thursday.
The plant is at Reliance's second petrochemicals facility at Hazira on the western coast.

"Historically, the global demand of polypropylene at 7.0 percent has been the fastest among all commodity plastics," it said. "In India, consumption has grown at an annual compounded rate of 22 percent over the past 10 years."
It estimated Indian demand for polypropylene in 1996/97 (April-March) at 425,000 tonnes. At present, almost 70 percent of the demand is met through imports, Reliance said.
The demand and supply are expected to be balanced at 540,000 tonnes during 1997/98. The only other producer is the state-run Indian Petrochemicals Corporation Ltd.
The international price of polypropylene is steady around $750-$800 per tonne cif, it said in a statement.
